summary: A free, compact urban park in Sam Yan with terraced lawns, ponds, paths and a distinctive water-management landscape. It is a worthwhile neighbourhood pause and a good way to see how Bangkok can combine recreation with flood-resilient green infrastructure.
whyGo: See an unusually legible example of landscape design that channels and stores rainwater as part of the park experience.
Take a relaxed walk, exercise, sit by the water or let children use the playground; it is an easy add-on to Sam Yan and Chula visits.
bestFor: A low-cost outdoor break close to MRT Sam Yan and the Chula-Sam Yan neighbourhood.
Visitors interested in contemporary landscape architecture, city parks or accessible family activities.
skipIf: You are looking for a large wilderness or a full-day destination; this is a small city park and usually works best as a short stop.
You need a guaranteed quiet visit: local exercise and community use can make the park lively, especially around cooler morning and evening periods.
duration: Allow about 45–90 minutes for an unhurried loop and a sit-down; this is a planning estimate, not an official visit duration.
cost: Entry is free. Chulalongkorn University lists underground parking at ฿20 for the first two hours and ฿20 per hour for hours 3–11; confirm rates on arrival. Transit fares are additional.
hours: The university currently lists daily opening hours of 05:00–22:00. Check its official page shortly before travel in case of maintenance, closures or event arrangements.
bestTime: Go early morning or from late afternoon into early evening for cooler temperatures and softer light. December is generally a more comfortable outdoor month than Bangkok's hot season, but shade and midday heat still matter.
gettingThere: The university's directions suggest MRT Sam Yan, Exit 2 at Chamchuri Square, then an 8–10 minute walk toward the university along Phaya Thai Road. BTS National Stadium, Exit 2, is another option, followed by a walk or bus along Rama I Road and a turn into Chulalongkorn Soi 5. Local buses also run along Rama I and Rama IV. The park has underground parking, but transit is simpler in central Bangkok.
booking: No booking is listed for ordinary public access. Special activities or organised events may have separate arrangements; check Chula's official park page and event notices before making a dedicated trip.
accessibility: Chulalongkorn University lists paths, ramps, seating, playgrounds, activity areas and restrooms. The site does not publish detailed route gradients, accessible toilet specifications or step-free transit connections, so confirm those details if they are essential.
practicalTips: Wear comfortable walking shoes; paths and open lawns are exposed, so bring water, sun protection and a hat.
Treat playgrounds, exercise spaces and restrooms as available facilities, while checking on arrival for maintenance or temporary closures.
For the simplest arrival, use MRT Sam Yan and follow the university's route from Exit 2; map apps may label the park by its Thai or English name.
decemberNotes: The park is listed as open daily, but no December 2026 programme or holiday schedule was confirmed. Chula's site describes community, health, arts and learning activities without promising particular dates. Check university announcements before travelling specifically for an event, and check hours again during the trip.
uncertainties: December 2026 event listings and any temporary holiday or maintenance closures were not available in the sources checked.
Published opening hours, parking fees and facilities may change before the trip.
